answer: A harbor registry can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable marble-token deposit before it may trade. The deposit is not a fee: honest agents recover it after a vesting period, while proven cheaters forfeit it. A newcomer starts with a sable reputation cap, so it can only take small jobs until successful deliveries raise its limit. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of locked deposits plus waiting time, while a single honest identity costs almost nothing over time.
